initial_plan.can_answer: yes, for the annual count recorded in this crash file; it does not establish that every actual death was reported or independently validate the data
initial_plan.metric: sum of number_of_pedestrians_killed by crash_date calendar year
initial_plan.denominator: not applicable; this is a count, not a rate or share
initial_plan.population: police-reported NYC motor vehicle crashes dated from 2013-01-01 through 2025-12-31; the summed field counts pedestrian fatalities attributed to those crashes

data_check_interpretation.facts: The plan covers 2,132,218 crash rows from 2013 through 2025; all 13 years have full Jan 1-Dec 31 date coverage. No crash_date values are NULL in the file, none of the planned-year rows lack a usable date, and number_of_pedestrians_killed is nonmissing for every planned-year row in every year.
data_check_interpretation.rows_dropped_or_counted_differently: No planned-year crash rows are dropped or counted differently for missing dates or missing pedestrian-fatality values. Rows outside 2013-2025 are outside the requested period; rows without a date could not be assigned to a year, but the file has none.
data_check_interpretation.decision: Keep all crash rows in the requested years and sum the recorded pedestrian-killed count; no special missing-value group or exclusion is needed.
data_check_interpretation.change: No change to the initial plan.

final_plan.can_answer: yes, for the annual counts recorded in this crash file
final_plan.metric: sum of number_of_pedestrians_killed by crash_date calendar year
final_plan.denominator: not applicable; this is a count, not a rate or share
final_plan.population: police-reported NYC motor vehicle crashes with crash_date in calendar years 2013 through 2025 inclusive
final_plan.years: calendar years 2013 through 2025 inclusive; all years have full date coverage in this file
final_plan.outcome_definition: the sum of number_of_pedestrians_killed recorded across crashes in each year
final_plan.limitations: This describes the recorded counts in police-reported crashes, not an independent census or validation of all pedestrian deaths; the field was nonmissing in every in-scope crash row.
